documents.unit: Office of the Provost, Division of Academic Affairs
documents.title: Statement on Academic Integrity and Use of Artificial Intelligence
documents.summary: A short provost statement from August 2024. Students may not use AI-assisted technology on graded work unless faculty authorize it, and faculty decide whether to allow AI and must state expectations in their syllabus. The rest is integrity framing and a promise to keep reviewing.
documents.stance_why: The statement says "students are not to use AI assisted technology in the classroom unless they are specifically authorized to do so by their faculty", a default ban with faculty-granted exceptions, so restrict. It is not delegates because it sets that university-wide default itself, and it names no tiers.

units.why: The opening frames AI as permanent ("here to stay") and as shaping education and work; it is a statement of purpose and context, so it is a framework preamble (P56) with informs modality rather than a rule. P44 does not fit because it teaches no AI skill.
units.anchor: These tools are here to stay and will continue to shape our futures

units.why: "obligation to complete our academic and scholarly work with absolute integrity and honesty" binds everyone and sets the principle behind the AI rule, so it is a general framework statement (P56), phrased as must.
units.anchor: obligation to complete our academic and scholarly work with absolute integrity and honesty

units.why: "We must always uphold our Community Standards and academic policies" ties AI use to existing integrity rules; I chose P36 (misconduct under existing processes) as the closest type, though it does not name sanctions explicitly.

"students are not to use AI assisted technology in the classroom unless they are specifically authorized" bans AI by default and permits it only with authorization, so P01 (default ban) with must-not; P06 is not chosen because the text is a general default, not a silent-syllabus rule.
units.anchor: students are not to use AI assisted technology in the classroom unless

units.why: "authorized to do so by their faculty for an assignment, a test, a quiz, or any deliverable" says permission comes from faculty per graded item; I chose P04 (instructor or assignment sets rule) because this is who decides, whereas the ban itself is the previous unit.
units.anchor: specifically authorized to do so by their faculty for an assignment, a test, a quiz
units.policy: Students may use AI-assisted technology only when their faculty specifically authorize it for an assignment, a test, a quiz, or any graded deliverable.

units.why: "We have much to learn" and "learning and sharing best practices" ask everyone to learn about AI and share practice; closest type is P63 (supporting learning about AI), though it addresses all rather than only faculty.
units.anchor: Let us all make sure we are learning and sharing best practices

units.why: "not allowing AI to do the learning for us" warns that AI should not substitute for learning, so it is the skill-building rationale (P41) with should-not; P32 (student stays primary solver) is close but the passage is framed as a learning rationale.
units.anchor: not allowing AI to do the learning for us

units.why: "whether you allow the use of generative AI or not in your classes is of course up to you" leaves the decision to each instructor, so P04 with may modality; it is addressed to faculty.
units.anchor: whether you allow the use of generative AI or not in your classes

units.why: "you should include a statement in your syllabus stating your expectations regarding student use of AI" directs faculty to put AI expectations in the syllabus, which is P09 with should modality.
units.anchor: you should include a statement in your syllabus stating your expectations

units.why: "Students, you came here for your own education. With this opportunity comes an important responsibility" appeals to students to own their education and honor tradition; closest is P29 (students are responsible for their work) with should.
units.anchor: Students, you came here for your own education
units.frag_end: excellence in all that you do.

units.why: "Loyola will continue evaluating and responding to the opportunities and challenges these tools present" commits the university to ongoing review, so P54 (revisit regularly) with informs.
units.anchor: Loyola will continue evaluating and responding to the opportunities and challenges these tools present

notes: Only one included document; no school or computing documents found. Topics vocabulary taken from codes used in other v2 outputs because AGENT_BRIEF.md is absent.
